name: Ghiyasuddin Azam Shah
seoTitle: Ghiyasuddin Azam Shah: Sultan of Bengal and Patron of Learning
seoDescription: Ghiyasuddin Azam Shah ruled Bengal around 1390–1410, strengthened the Iliyas Shahi state, patronised literature, and opened diplomatic exchanges with China.
contribution: Ghiyasuddin Azam Shah was the third sultan of the early Iliyas Shahi dynasty. His reign focused more on consolidating Bengal than on extended conquest, although sources associate him with a campaign into Kamarupa. He is also remembered for patronising scholars and for supporting Shah Muhammad Sagir's Yusuf-Zulekha.
context: Bengal's late-fourteenth- and early-fifteenth-century sultanate, when court culture in Pandua and Sonargaon connected Islamic learning, Bengali literature, Persianate scholarship, and regional diplomacy.
impact: Ghiyasuddin's court helped make Sonargaon a centre of Persian learning and literary activity. He corresponded with the Persian poet Hafiz and sent diplomatic missions to China in 1405, 1408, and 1409, showing that the Bengal sultanate participated in wider intellectual and commercial networks beyond the subcontinent.
